title: 3.7.22 Lab: Array-Methods Capstone
description: Combine the module's non-mutating tools: build a list, transform it with .map(), take a range with .slice(), join with .concat() or spread, and copy an object with an override. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build a source list
steps.instructions: Create a variable (the lesson calls it prices; use any name that fits) and fill it with at least five numbers, using prices.push() as you build.

steps.title: Transform with .map()
steps.instructions: Use .map() to build a new array (the lesson calls it bumped) where every price is increased by a fixed amount or percentage. Decimal results can print with a long tail of digits (such as 55.00000000000001); that is how computers store decimals, not a mistake.

steps.title: Take a range with .slice()
steps.instructions: Use .slice() to copy a part of bumped into a variable (the lesson calls it middle).

steps.title: Join two arrays
steps.instructions: Create a second array and join it with middle using .concat() or array spread, into a variable (the lesson calls it joined).

steps.title: Copy an object with an override
steps.instructions: Create an object with at least two properties, then build a copy with one property changed using object spread and an override. Log it alongside the original.

steps.title: Log every result
steps.instructions: Use console.log for the transformed, sliced and joined arrays and for both objects. Confirm the original prices array still holds its starting values.

requirements.title: prices built with .push()
requirements.description: Declares prices as an array and adds to it with prices.push(). Help: 3.3.2 (Array Basics: Index, push, pop)
requirements.hint: Start prices as an empty array and add each value with prices.push(...), one call per value. A push onto some other array does not build prices.

requirements.title: .map() used
requirements.description: Calls .map() to transform the list. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Use .map on prices with a function that increases each price, and keep the result in a second variable.

requirements.title: .slice() used
requirements.description: Calls .slice() to copy a range. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Use .slice with a start and an end index to copy part of the transformed array.

requirements.title: Arrays joined
requirements.description: Joins two arrays with .concat() or array spread. Help: 3.7.9 (Joining Lists with .concat())
requirements.hint: Join two arrays with .concat, or with both spread inside new square brackets.

requirements.title: Object spread with override
requirements.description: Builds an object copy with a property written after the spread. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Copy an object with spread in braces and write the changed property after the spread.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Log the arrays, both objects, and the original prices to confirm it did not change.

requirements.title: prices holds five or more numbers, and bumped, middle and joined are made from it
requirements.description: prices is an array of at least five numbers, bumped is a changed copy of it, middle a part of bumped, joined holds middle and more, and the output shows them. Help: 3.7.20 (Chaining .map() off a .push()-Built Array)
requirements.hint: Build prices with five or more numbers using push, then print the three arrays, both objects and the original prices.

checks.fail: prices needs five or more numbers, each added with push.
bumped should be a changed copy of prices made with .map(): the same length, with the numbers changed, while prices keeps its own values.

requirements.title: every result is made from prices and printed by code that runs
requirements.description: When prices holds other numbers, bumped, middle and joined change with it, and console.log calls that run print them, prices, and both objects. Help: 3.7.20 (Chaining .map() off a .push()-Built Array)
requirements.hint: Make each array from the one before it (map, then slice, then concat or spread), and print every result, prices and both objects. Numbers typed in by hand, or typed-in output, do not change when prices does.

checks.fail: bumped has to be computed from prices with .map(): when the checker changes prices, bumped must change with them. Numbers typed in by hand stay the same.
middle has to be sliced out of bumped: when bumped changes, middle must change with it. A list typed in by hand stays the same.
joined has to be built from middle: when middle changes, joined must hold the changed values. A list typed in by hand stays the same.
Print bumped with console.log, by code that runs. Typed-in text does not count.
Print middle itself, console.log(middle), with a console.log that runs. Printing bumped or joined shows the same values but is not the slice.
Print joined itself, console.log(joined), with a console.log that runs. Printing middle and the other array is not the joined list.
Print prices too, console.log(prices), so the output shows the original still holds its starting values.
Print both objects, the copy with the override and the original, each with a console.log that runs.
The copy with the override has to be spread from your object: when the checker changes the object's values, the copy's other values must change too. An object typed in by hand stays the same.
